holidays.name: I Love Lucy Day
holidays.description: Fans of the classic sitcom celebrate Lucy Ricardo's slapstick chaos. Popular ways to mark the day include a marathon of episodes, a plate of chocolates on a conveyor belt, or a bit of grape stomping.
holidays.origin: The date marks the night in 1951 when I Love Lucy first aired on CBS. The show starred Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz and became one of the most beloved comedies in television history.
holidays.funFact: I Love Lucy was one of the first major sitcoms filmed in front of a live studio audience on 35mm film. That's a big reason the episodes still look crisp and are rerun around the world decades later.

holidays.name: National Grouch Day
holidays.description: This is a day for the cranky, the curmudgeonly and the perpetually unimpressed. Grumbling is encouraged, and you can complain about the weather, traffic or Mondays without apology.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and it is often linked to Oscar the Grouch of Sesame Street. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Oscar the Grouch was originally orange when Sesame Street debuted in 1969. He turned green before the show's second season.
